summary.text: PA6-CF is carbon-fibre-filled PA6, a semicrystalline polyamide. Makers sell it for fixtures, clamps and structural parts used in dry environments. Its HDT at 0.45 MPa is 193 °C, well above its glass transition. On the H2C every product needs a hardened nozzle, Bambu Lab's guide requires an enclosure, and most products call for drying at 65⁠–⁠110 °C, 4⁠–⁠12 h.

items.text: Similar to other Bambu CF Filaments, these outstanding mechanical properties make it an ideal choice for printing fixtures, clamps, automotive and mechanical components and various structural and engineering parts that used in dry environments.
The carbon fiber reinforcement provides significantly high stiffness and strength properties in dry environments and maintains exceptional heat resistance and impact resistance.

Bambu PA6-CF will experience a decrease in strength and stiffness after absorbing water, making it not recommended for printing models with high requirements for strength, stiffness, and dimensional stability, especially thin and elongated models. The prints of PA6-CF usually become tougher and more resistant to impacts, drops, and collisions when they get damp; you can dampen and soften the prints in advance if the model requires high toughness.

items.agent: Water or aqueous solutions at high temperature
items.text: All polyamides take up water when kept in a moist environment. At room temperature this is a physical process which is reversible. Irreversible chemical damage to the material can only be caused by water or aqueous solutions at high temperatures. This is referred to as hydrolysis. Water uptake is mainly dependent on the amide group concentration of the individual polyamide type. For this reason, polyamide 12 is considerably more resistant to hydrolysis than polyamide 6 and polyamide 66.
